result:
Round 7 (S1, S2 and S3) is implemented, but one drift requirement (RF7-2) failed in my own runs, so bug C-R6-02 stays open. Everything else is waiting for C. I claim no PASS.

The previous session did all the work and was restarted during its final check. This session changed no code. I re-ran every gate on the current tree and added the results to the report as ┬º11, at `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-7.md`.

**Gates (re-run now):**
- **Types and tests:** `tsc` exit 0; vitest 779 of 779 passed (761 before + 18 new).
- **Biome:** 0 errors on my files and on `./app` (`./app` has 218 warnings, the same count as in C's round 6).
- **Build:** passes.
- **Protected files:** all 4 hashes match. `Header.tsx` has no diff, and `position-store.ts`, `video-sync.ts` and `types/arrangement.ts` are unchanged.
- **Scope:** `git status` shows 14 modified and 2 new files, all from the files B allowed. No round-6 work was reverted, and nothing was committed.

**What changed (from the earlier session):**
- **S1 (C-R6-02, drift):** the playhead, ruler playhead, transport time and video gap time now update the page directly each frame instead of re-rendering React. Per-frame cost at the median went from 2.0 ms to 0.7ΓÇô0.8 ms. Follow no longer reads `scrollLeft` right after writing it, and the overview no longer updates React state while scrolling. Ruler ticks and library rows are memoised so they don't re-render on Play. My Play-click measurement went from a median of 22.1 ms to 10.8 ms. That was click-plus-render time, not the long-frame number C will measure.
- **S2 (C-R6-03, ruler):** a new label-fit rule drops any ruler label that would not fit inside the timeline. In the browser the overflow was 0ΓÇô1 px in C's cases at both screen sizes.
- **S3 (C-R6-01, Volume):** a Volume slider drag now claims the gesture registry. Blur or pointer cancel reverts it and writes no history, a refused drag snaps back with the status message, and closing the workspace releases the claim. Three of the new tests failed when I temporarily put back the round-6 slider code, so they do catch the old bug.

**Not ready on my own evidence:**
- **RF7-2:** R2-V3 run V3_2 failed with 0.1203 s drift. It had no long frame attributed to the app, and I didn't find the cause within the run budget. I have no before-fix R2-V3 runs. All 3 R3-V1 runs passed before and after the fix.
- **RF7-3:** C's failure (video not starting after the loop runs) did not reproduce in 3 attempts, so I made no change for it.
- **Not run by me:** real-mouse and real-focus checks; the adjacent regressions R10-N6, R4-M2, R26-* in the browser, and R27-1; Fit on 4 and 20 minutes.

**Review:** the code-reviewer subagent ran once and scored the change 7/10. I fixed H1, M1ΓÇôM4, L1, L2 and L7. I didn't apply L5, because it would suppress the refusal status the task requires. The reviewer was not re-run on those fixes.

**Notes for B and C:**
- **L3 (B):** the ruler tick step does not guarantee room for the label at very low zoom, for example "10:00" at 4 px/s.
- **LoAF collector (C):** C's current long-frame collector doesn't record forced-layout time, which RF7-P1 needs. The report shows how to add it.
- **Carried findings:** the remaining items from the root pre-push review and the publication checkpoint are listed in report ┬º10.
